items.title: Louie Bellson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: So I did about five weeks with that band and recorded with them.

ctx.x: The first time with Basie? Let me see. It was actually when I joined Norman Granz, Jazz at the Philharmonic. I had known Basie before that because in 1951 he’d been appearing in New York at the Strand Theater and we were at Birdland, right across the street. And he used to come down and his own words were “I went straight to the bar and put my head down and with my hands around my head, and just listened to you guys, and getting madder and madder as I heard all of this great music coming out of that band.” You…

we’ll fix it out Lou, I’ll take care of your guys and you can play the gig when you get back.” So I did about five weeks with that band and recorded with them. And that was like Ellington’s band, just a tremendous experience. I was talking to Frank Wess about that today because he was on the band, and also Benny Powell. And Basie during that time was trying to straighten himself out, not too much alcohol. And he knew that I didn’t drink and I had some goodies in my bag at all times to munch on. Because over there…

items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Then I had a chance to go to Europe with Basie. Sonny Payne got sick. I recorded with Basie – did an album with him.

ctx.x: Who else was in the band other than Charlie Shavers?

Let me see. Who else was in that band? He was the only big star. The other guys were all good players, but Charlie was the main key. Then I had a chance to go to Europe with Basie. Sonny Payne got sick. I recorded with Basie – did an album with him. Then we left for Europe. I was supposed to go into Birdland with my small band, but they cancelled that out so I could help Basie out in Europe. That was six weeks there. Oh boy. That was a lot of fun. Thad Jones was in the band. Al Grey, Frank . . .
